sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Thermoforming and Automated Trimming of Multilayer Aligners

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition) with a special statutory regime for Private Interest Foundations and Anglo-American trust influences in foundation practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 2012)
European Union–Central America Association Agreement (in force for Panama 2013)
Panama–Costa Rica Free Trade Agreement (in force 2019)
Bilateral Investment Treaties in force with Germany, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Spain, France, South Korea, and Argentina
Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements in force with Mexico, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015, as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019 and Ley No. 254 de 2022 (Panama AML/CFT statute); Decreto Ejecutivo No. 406 de 22 de mayo de 2019; Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 on Private Interest Foundations; and the Beneficial Owner Registry regulations administered by the Registro Público de Panamá.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Foundation Charter (Carta Fundacional) setting out founder, foundation purpose, initial endowment, registered office and foundation council
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public and Registro Público de Panamá
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial authentication and Public Registry filing; no apostille required for registration in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Existence of Corporate Founder (if the founder is a foreign legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or statutory authority in the founder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions, followed by notarized Spanish translation in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Acceptance of Appointment by Foundation Council Members and any Protector; including beneficial ownership declaration where the council member is a legal representative of a UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of residence of the relevant individual or entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus certified Spanish translation by a Panamanian public translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Declaration of Ultimate Beneficial Owner (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) identifying all natural persons holding directly or indirectly 25% or more control or ownership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foundation founder through the resident agent; filed with the Registro Público de Panamá UBO module
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in Panama and electronically filed with the Public Registry's Beneficial Owner Register

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and continuing screening of founders, foundation council members, protectors, authorized persons, and all ultimate beneficial owners against OFAC SDN, UN Consolidated Sanctions, EU Consolidated Sanctions, Panamanian Public Registry blocking lists, domestic designated terrorist lists, and local/foreign PEP databases. Any PEP or sanctioned person triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, senior-management approval, and if applicable a suspicious transaction report to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) of Panama. A confirmed sanctions match is an automatic basis for client refusal.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Sistema de Certificado y Reserva de Nombre en Línea via https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must be distinguishable and expressed in the Spanish alphabet. A Private Interest Foundation must include the legal identifier 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'FIP'. Foreign-language names are accepted only when transliterated compatibly with Spanish and when no registered or reserved identical or confusingly similar name exists.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A valid name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days by online request before expiry. If the Reserva de Nombre is rejected, the resident agent or incorporated attorney may file a written 'recurso de reconsideración' with the Dirección General de Personas Jurídicas of the Registro Público within five (5) business days of notification; a second administrative appeal and ultimately judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia remain available upon exhaustion of administrative remedies. In practice, the applicant should simultaneously reserve a commercially acceptable alternative name to prevent registration delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible to satisfy the formal registered-office requirement through a licensed resident agent, but it is not a substitute for physical commercial substance in the claimed ISIC 3250 thermoforming and trimming of clear dental aligner sheets. If the PIF engages in real manufacturing, DGI and municipal authorities will require a physical operating establishment, municipal aviso de operación, sanitary and medical-device registrations, and demonstrable staff, equipment, and inventory at that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 40% for an active manufacturing PIF within the first twelve months due to industrial, municipal, and sanitary inspections; approximately 10% for a PIF used as a passive holding or group structure with a registered office only.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Online name search, certificate of name availability, and 30-day name reservation with the Registro Público de Panamá
Preparation of Foundation Charter, foundation regulations, and governance paperwork by licensed Panamanian counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for professional services, not a statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Foundation Charter and UBO Declaration before a Panamanian notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee schedule plus notary expenses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry registration, stamp law, and corporate formality fees for the Private Interest Foundation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff and stamp duties

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Year-one registered agent / resident agent retainer required under Law 25 of 1995
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; mandatory service under Panamanian foundation law

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO Register filing and PEP/OFAC/UN sanctions screening performed by the compliance officer and resident agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for AML/CFT compliance services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization bundle for foreign corporate/founder documents plus certified Spanish translation in Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign Ministry of document origin and Panamanian certified public translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular/apostille fees plus market translation fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative statutory fee and professional filing fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Ley No. 2 de 2011, Ley No. 13 de 2015 and Ley No. 72 de 2017), Articles 1-10 (charter contents), Article 20 (registry inscription), and Article 23 (initial patrimony).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Panama City, Republic of Panama
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (Private Interest Foundation Charter executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Public Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The foundation must declare a minimum founding patrimony of US$10,000 (B/.10,000). Law 25 of 1995 does not require immediate full payment into an escrow account at formation; the charter must state the composition and value of the endowment, and the assets must be lawfully owned or controlled by the foundation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED by the Foundation Council of the Private Interest Foundation incorporated under Law 25 of 1995, as follows: First, the Council accepts the initial endowment of US$10,000 declared in the foundation charter and acknowledges the Founder's contribution. Second, the registered office is fixed at the address of the Resident Agent in Panama City, Republic of Panama. Third, the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual meeting, with full authority over foundation assets, accounts, and seal. Fourth, the Council ratifies the opening of statutory books and instructs the Resident Agent to obtain the tax identification number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney and registered Resident Agent, subject to supervision by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) under Law 23 of 2015
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Acta Constitutiva in Spanish. The attorney verifies the founder's identity, performs customer due diligence required by Law 23 of 2015, and defines the foundation purpose as the manufacture and commercialization of thermoformed dental clear aligner sheets and related orthodontic devices. The charter must name the founder, initial Foundation Council members, Resident Agent, reserved rights of the founder or beneficiaries, and the initial patrimony of US$10,000.
required_dossiers: Copy of founder's passport or foundation/corporate resolution if the founder is a legal person
Proof of the initial endowment or asset declaration
Certificate of good standing of any corporate founder
AML/CFT intake form (UAF-compliant)
Power of attorney to the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the attorney identifies discrepancies in the endowment evidence or AML documentation, the founder is granted 5 business days to provide curative documents; otherwise the filing is suspended until compliance is achieved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Circuito de Panamá (Public Notary of the Judicial Circuit of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange attendance of the founder or authorized representative and the Resident Agent before the notary. The charter is read aloud, signed, and the notary authenticates the act and the signatures. The notary issues certified testimonios which serve as the official instrument for registry inscription.
required_dossiers: Executed foundation charter draft
Valid passport or national ID of all signatories
Resident Agent's notarized acceptance
Payment of notarial fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to any clause or purpose, the attorney revises the charter and a new execution is requested within 3 business days; the defective original is voided and re-executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Public Registry Inscription of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized testimonio to the Foundation Section together with the treasury fee payment. The Registrar examines the deed for legal compliance and statutory fee deposits. Upon approval, the foundation receives an inscription number and acquires separate legal personality; a certified copy is returned for the statutory books.
required_dossiers: Notarized testimonio of the Acta Constitutiva
Registry fee payment receipt (approximately US$250)
Certified copy of the charter for sealing
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a reparo (defect note) is issued, the attorney files a written subsanación with the Registrar within 10 business days and pays the re-examination fee; the corrected file is prioritized within the next 3 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification (RUC) and Municipal Operating Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance; Alcaldía de Panamá (Municipality of Panama) via the Ventanilla Única
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the inscribed charter, apply through the DGI Sede Electrónica for the Registro Único de Contribuyente, selecting the economic activity Manufacture of Medical Devices (ISIC 3250). The municipal Aviso de Operación is obtained through the municipality's Single Business Window; employer registration with the Caja de Seguro Social is initiated simultaneously.
required_dossiers: Inscribed foundation charter and Registry certificate
Resident Agent's identification and accreditation
RUC application form
Aviso de Operación application and municipal fee receipt
Governing council resolution confirming the administrator and fiscal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects the ISIC code or requests prior industrial authorization, the applicant obtains a provisional RUC referencing pending industrial validation and completes the MICI license before the DGI finalizes permanent registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Environmental and Sanitary Licensing Intake
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección Nacional de Industrias; Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) - Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the industrial registration (Registro Industrial) to MICI describing thermoforming and automated trimming capacity. File the environmental registration or EIA with MiAMBIENTE according to the determined category. Submit the medical-device notification and sanitary operation permit application to MINSA under Executive Decree No. 1601 of 2012, classifying dental clear aligners as Class II devices. Commercial manufacturing may not commence before all authorizations are issued.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate and Registry certificate
Foundation charter and officer identification
Facility layout and equipment list (thermoformers, CNC trimmers, wash stations)
Product dossier, specifications, and material safety data sheets (PETG, EVA or TPU sheets)
Environmental registration form or EIA scope for Categoría II
Fire safety certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos
Waste management plan and solvent inventory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MINSA defers or classifies the product as a higher-risk device, the manufacturer may appeal to the National Directorate of Pharmacy and Drugs within 10 business days and re-file with supplemental technical or clinical evidence. If MiAMBIENTE issues observations, a corrective environmental management plan is submitted within 15 business days instead of outright denial.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección Nacional de Industrias, in coordination with Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) - Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas and the Municipality of Panama for the Aviso de Operación
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Industrial (MICI), Municipal Aviso de Operación, and MINSA Sanitary Operation Permit / Medical Device Registration (Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento) for Class II dental clear aligner manufacturing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I (Registro Ambiental) under Executive Decree 123 of 2002, elevated to Categoría II (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental General) if solvent/VOC emissions exceed 25 metric tons per year or if wastewater discharge volumes exceed the municipal collection capacity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent limits per Executive Decree No. 75 of 2018: pH 6-9, BOD5 less than or equal to 40 mg/L, COD less than or equal to 150 mg/L, total suspended solids less than or equal to 35 mg/L; atmospheric emissions per the national air quality regulation (Executive Decree No. 5 of 2001) with activated carbon or best-available-control-technology VOC abatement; hazardous waste (spent solvents, plastic scrap, waste aligners) managed under Law No. 24 of 2007 and implementing regulations using licensed waste transporters and manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá annual fire-prevention certificate covering thermoforming heat zones, electrical panels and compressed-air systems; municipal structural load and occupancy certificate for the production floor; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) workplace hygiene and safety clearance addressing noise, heat and airborne plastic particulates; employer registration with the Caja de Seguro Social for industrial accident coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – General Directorate of Revenue of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF); electronic portal: SITIO (Sistema Integrado de Información Tributaria), https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation (PIF) under Law 25 of 1995: (1) execute the Foundation Charter before a Panamanian notary through a licensed Foundation Agent and register it in the Public Registry of Panama; (2) after issuance of the Foundation Certificate, apply to the DGI for a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) via SITIO or in-person filing, submitting the foundation certificate, agent appointment, registered address, beneficial-owner declaration (Law 254 of 2021), and director identification; (3) obtain an electronic signature (firma electrónica) and VAT/ITBMS activation; (4) file the Aviso de Operación with the Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) and obtain the municipal business license for the manufacturing plant; (5) appoint a Panama-licensed CPA as statutory fiscal representative. RUC issuance typically takes 10–20 business days; the RUC is mandatory for any Panamanian-source taxable activity while foreign-source asset holding and income remain entirely outside the Panamanian tax base without additional registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box or entity-classification election; the PIF is a separate legal person taxed strictly on territorial-source income (only Panamanian-source profits at 25% corporate rate; foreign-source income is excluded). The Foundation Charter may elect between trust-like or corporation-like administration rules for private law. Available tax elections include voluntary ITBMS registration for taxpayers below the B/. 36,000 threshold, accelerated depreciation for manufacturing machinery, the SEM (Multinational Headquarters) regime under Law 41 of 2007 if qualifying services are rendered, and free-zone/Panama-Pacifico designation if the production plant is relocated to an export-processing zone. Panama has not enacted OECD hybrid-mismatch or check-the-box legislation; Pillar Two GloBE rules apply only to MNE groups with EUR 750 million+ consolidated revenue from fiscal year 2025.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's value-added tax) under Law 28 of 1995, as amended (Law 8 of 2010 and Law 191 of 2021)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 36,000 (Panamanian Balboa at 1:1 parity with USD) of annual gross turnover from taxable Panamanian-source activities; taxpayers below the threshold may register voluntarily as minor contributors
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) pursuant to DGI Resolution No. 201-4727 of 2020: all RUC holders must issue standardized XML invoices through the SITIO 2.0 web services (REST API) which validate, timestamp, and return a fiscal authorization with a QR code and consecutive number. Large taxpayers (Segment A) transmit and obtain fiscal clearance in real time before delivery; medium and small taxpayers (Segments B/C) transmit within the month under the phased rollout completed by June 2025. Export e-invoices must cross-reference the customs export declaration and are individually validated by the DGI before zero-rating is accepted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods manufactured in Panama — including ISIC 3250 thermoplastic dental clear-aligner sheets (HS Chapters 3920/3921 and, if finished, 9021) — qualify for 0% ITBMS under Article 62(2) of Law 28 of 1995 provided: (a) the seller holds a valid RUC; (b) the goods physically leave Panamanian customs territory; (c) the export e-invoice carries the zero-rated exemption code; and (d) proceeds are repatriated and evidenced within the statutory period. Offshore services rendered to non-residents for use entirely abroad may also be zero-rated; local-term services remain at 7%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUA – Declaración Única Aduanera (single customs export declaration filed through Panama Customs VUCE/SISCO system with HS classification and declared value)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing physical removal from Panamanian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa) issued by the receiving bank confirming credit of export proceeds
Commercial invoice with Incoterms, zero-rated ITBMS annotation, QR-code e-invoice number and export license/reference
Packing list and certificate of origin (where preferential tariff treatment is claimed)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and Panama Customs audit export zero-rating claims under Articles 699–713 and 760 of the Código Fiscal and DGI Resolution No. 201-4256/2019. Fraudulent or substantively deficient claims trigger retrospective clawback of the 7% ITBMS, monthly default interest, fines of 50%–100% of the omitted tax, RUC suspension or cancellation, and criminal liability for tax fraud under Penal Code Article 258-A (as amended by Law 8 of 2010) with imprisonment of 2–5 years. Exporters must retain the complete supporting documentation bundle for at least 7 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama does not operate a central bank. The monetary and prudential oversight of banks, trust, and finance companies is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP - Superintendency of Banks of Panama), while macro-financial and exchange-related statistics are maintained by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and, for financial intelligence, the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (Financial Analysis Unit - UAF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy. The US dollar is legal tender, and the Panamanian Balboa is a subsidiary, fixed-at-par accounting unit used only for fractional local coins. There is no practical distinction between the current and capital account: transfers of principal, profits, dividends, and loan repayments can be freely routed through USD-denominated bank accounts without any special administrative conversion. No Central Bank pre-approval exists because there is no central monetary authority. The only repartriation hurdle is not exchange-based but tax-based: a Panamanian-registered PIF owning a Panamanian permanent establishment for manufacturing dental aligner sheets must apply the cannotoon-territorial income tax and withhold tax on dividends paid or remitted to resident or non-resident beneficiaries. Where no economic activity is carried out inside Panama, the PIF receives and distributes income without any foreign exchange authorisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation exists. Panamanian law does not require any conversion ratio, time-level pre-negotiation, or foreign exchange retention limit. Exporting entities and PIFs may hold USD proceeds onshore or offshore indefinitely. To satisfy banking AML/CFT expectations, the PIF exporting thermoformed aligner sheets must retain the underlying shipment invoice, bill of lading, and customs export document (Certificado de Re-exportación or via DUA - Declaración Única de Aduanas) for at least 5 years, as required under SBP Resolution No. 2018-49-010 and Law 23 of 2015 on money laundering and terrorist financing.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Corporate Account / Foreign Trade Execution Account
Operational USD Account with Integrated Clearing and Trade Finance
Current Account / Capital Escrow Account for Yield-bearing Deposits
Multicurrency Operational Account and Trade Finance Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with strict overlay on top of traditional banking. Under Panamanian Decree-Law 2 of 2008 as updated by IBC Law 4 of 2020 and SBP Payment Regulation No. 005-2022, non-bank electronic money issuers and payment service providers (fintech/EMIs) must be licensed locally to custody funds and provide payment services. Foreign offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK or Eurozone EMI passports) do not enjoy direct passporting rights into Panama. They may be used as settlement vehicles exclusively for platform card acquisition (Stripe/PayPal) when the PIF has an established originating bank relationship, but cannot replace a licensed Panamanian commercial bank for holding the PIF's operating liquidity or executing MT103 trade payments. Any PIF that uses an unlicensed EMI for initial capital contribution will likely invoke KYC rejection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one signatory director (usually the Foundation Council officer or the Registered Agent's authorised officer) is a de facto mandate for most tier-1 Panamanian banks except for certain private and fintech-adjacent firms. Entities incorporated as PIFs are treated as customer-prestige vehicles, not as banking customers with automatic remote on-boarding. Remote account opening is possible at Global Bank and Multibank only when the foundation deed has been authenticated with a notarial apostille, the Registered Agent (a Panama law firm) submits an electronic KYC pack signed with a digital certificate, and the final executive director completes a video interview. Banco General and Banco Nacional generally require an in-person interview at a branch or a very senior private banker referral.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The PIF's beneficial owner is not a legally identified natural person, or the Banking Act need-to-know under Article 6 of Law 23 of 2015 cannot be satisfied.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full legalised copy of the Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) and the Foundation Regulations; a sworn disclosure of the Beneficial Owner and Foundation Council Members on the SBP-approved Form (Formulario D); a certificate of good standing from the Registry of Private Interest Foundations of Panama; and a notarized statement from the Registered Agent identifying the settlor, foundation council, guardian, and beneficiaries with passport copies for each natural person named as beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The declared ISIC 3250 (dental clear aligner sheets) is considered low-risk, but the manufacturing nature of the entity requires a physical inventory, production facility, and sanitary license; otherwise, the byproduct-target customer can be confused with a passive rentier treaty FI.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a detailed business plan with factory lease agreement in an industrial park; a copy of the medical device or industrial manufacturing registration (or a certificate of exclusion) from the Ministry of Health – Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas; an environmental (or contingency) permit from the Municipality; and at least two purchase orders from licensed orthodontic distributors to prove real commercial operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large unexpected inbound contribution from an offshore affiliate or from an unrelated founder who appears only as the endorsee of the PIF's initial asset (USD 10.00 - 10,000 min). This triggers the 'origin of funds' red-flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble the source-of-wealth statement of the contributing founder (pay stubs, dividend vouchers, sale and purchase agreements); a copy of the underlying SWIFT or international wire instruction showing the legal sender and the PIF as beneficiary; and, if the transfer is executed via the PIF's own liquidation from a former corporate shell, a winding-up and dissolution statement from the prior jurisdiction evidencing that assets have been lawfully transferred.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The PIF's initial and subsequent capital injections, including founder contributions and inter-affiliate funding, must be routed via the SWIFT network using an MT103 payment order from the remitter's commercial bank to a Panamanian tier-1 bank. The message field 70 (remittance information) must quote e.g., 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – PIF PA_PIF – INVOICE/AGREEMENT 001'. For transfers from a non-resident shareholder, cite the source of funds in field 72 to pre-empt AML review. If the injection exceeds USD 100,000, the International Private Banking department of the receiving bank may request a Compliance Certificate and the foundation's own balance sheet. All inbound funds are tagged as 'patrimonial asset' of the PIF and not as ordinary income for territorial tax purposes, provided no local business activity occurs in Panama.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade payments for imported PETG, copolyester pallets, CNC tools, and packaging materials must be cleared either through local ACH (ACH Panama) for domestic counterparties or, for cross-border suppliers, via SWIFT MT103 with a standard 'T1' misinformation or a commercial LC. For high-value consignment (over USD 250,000), the shipment database should be synchronized to an irrevocable sight Letter of Credit issued by Banco General or Global Bank in favor of the foreign die-cutting supplier. All outbound disbursements must carry the customs preamble: 'PAN-ADV-2025-XXXXX', the commercial invoice, and the PIF's RUC.
